items.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016
items.q: Because my colleagues like Bill Dobbins and Jeff Campbell and Danko... I’ve become a lot more informed. I realized how uninformed I was being at Eastman.

ctx.x: But where were you with the theoretical part of teaching jazz?

I was in a pretty good place with that. I’d been teaching a lot at some of the schools in Los Angeles — at USC and Cal Arts and I taught at a school called the Colburn School which is more of a classical school, and in terms of — well I don’t think you’re talking specifically like music theory, but I have a degree in music theory and so the theoretical, like harmony, like very specific harmony things, I was pretty good, I was pretty informed. But I’ve become a lot more informed. I realized how uninformed I was…
Okay I want you to think back — well I’m not sure when this would be — but did you have a specific moment or moments of inspiration that led you down the jazz path?
